statement: Sourced knowledge systems can preserve multiple conflicting assertions and contextual qualifiers without choosing a single truth.
actakit_implication: ActaKit should store source-bounded claims and contradictions, not a universal truth value.

statement: Some qualifiers are meaning-changing, especially time, jurisdiction and scope.
actakit_implication: Pre-SQL fixtures must test whether claim scope needs explicit structured qualifiers, but avoid a universal qualifier graph.

statement: A claim should remain meaningful and verifiable even when machine-readable context is absent.
actakit_implication: Structured qualifiers/enrichments should augment rather than define the proposition.

statement: A sourced knowledge system may legitimately preserve multiple contradictory values and explicitly states that references identify sources rather than world truth.
actakit_implication: Do not collapse contradictory civic claims into one current truth row; preserve source-bounded assertions and relations.

statement: Merge requires strong identity confidence and obsolete identifiers are redirected rather than reused.
actakit_implication: Entity merges must preserve lineage/tombstone mapping and never recycle old local IDs.

statement: Time, method and scope can materially qualify an assertion without requiring the assertion itself to disappear.
actakit_implication: Allow a bounded structured scope/qualifier mechanism when fixtures prove it changes claim meaning; do not universalize Wikidata snaks.

statement: Source references and preferred/current consensus are separate concepts.
actakit_implication: Review/assessment must not be encoded as provenance or source strength.
